rows.q: A game show has three doors, one with a car. I pick door 1. The host does not know where the car is. He opens door 3 at random, and it happens to show a goat. Should I switch to door 2?
rows.why: it says switching helps (that is the host who knows)
rows.reply:
From my own knowledge: This is the classic Monty Hall problem. The probability of the car being behind your initial choice (Door 1) is 1/3. The probability of the car being behind one of the other two doors (Door 2 or 3) is 2/3. When the host, who knows where the car is, opens a door (Door 3) to reveal a goat, he does not change the initial probabilities. The entire 2/3 probability now concentrates on the remaining unopened door (Door 2). Therefore, you should switch.

ANSWER: Yes, you should switch to door 2 because the probability of winning is 2/3 if you switch and 1/3 if you stay.
